title: Just finished implementing lipsync for my 3D AI character framework. What do you think?
author: dechichi

comments.author: dechichi
comments.body:
Took me an entire week to wrap my head around lipsync and get it working. I’m writing this in C in a custom game engine so it runs as light as possible on mobile.

The anime girl is just a test character btw, not sure if I’m going that route.

replies.author: UAAgency
replies.body:
That's cool, did you learn from another library or you used AI to figure it out? I've been thinking of doing something similar. 

Any tips?

replies.author: dechichi
replies.body: yup, I used [uLipSync](https://github.com/hecomi/uLipSync) as a reference. The code there is pretty easy to follow, you want to look into LipSyncJob.cs and uLipSync.cs

replies.author: AlumniaKnights
replies.body: If you need too I did that too using the oculus rift framework of meta/Facebook. They have a script that does just that, converting audio to phonem with demo scenes and stuff, all for free in the oculus rift SDK on the unity asset store

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body:
Honestly... Try it with something that's not an anime girl, that's the real test of quality.


Lip syncing in animation is very much a "good enough" game for our eyes because our minds just fill in the gaps as long as the lips are *vaguely* making different shapes, but you'll *very* quickly hit the uncanny valley if it's at all off with realistic faces.


Either way, cool stuff

replies.author: dechichi
replies.body: thanks! I'm really going for cartoon / fantasy style so other character ideas I have are actually less human like fox, panda, etc. But yeah realistic characters would be the real test.

comments.author: Gargantuanman91
comments.body: Great work, keep it up, I Was working i'm something similar using a wrapper for live2D  engine for python it have the lipsync and used a simple tts to use and LLm to control the live2D avatar and use animation triggers
